## Greptile Summary

This PR addresses a user experience issue where the Storybook upgrade process was reformatting package.json files by converting tab indentation to 2-space indentation. The fix modifies the `writePackageJson` method in the `JsPackageManager` class to preserve the original indentation style of package.json files.

The change introduces the `detect-indent` package to analyze the existing package.json file's indentation pattern before writing the updated version. Instead of always using a hardcoded 2-space indentation (`JSON.stringify(packageJsonToWrite, null, 2)`), the code now:

1. Reads the existing package.json file content
2. Uses `detect-indent` to determine the current indentation style (tabs, 2 spaces, 4 spaces, etc.)
3. Preserves that detected indentation when writing the updated package.json

This fix is part of the core package manager functionality that handles package.json modifications during Storybook upgrades. The `JsPackageManager` class is a foundational component used across different package managers (npm, yarn, pnpm) to handle package.json operations, making this fix universally applicable to all Storybook upgrade scenarios.

comments.author: Sidnioulz
comments.body:
It's potentially risky to read the local package.json, because scripts could use `writePackageJson` to move a package.json to a new location.

You could make the code more robust locally by encapsulating the indent computation in a try catch (and defaulting to 2 on catch). This way, for all use cases where we modify a packageJson in place, it'd work; and for other use cases, it wouldn't crash.

If you're up for it, you could also compute indentation in the code paths that _load_ packageJsons and add it to the object with a Symbol (e.g. `[Symbol.for('indent')]: detectIndent(...)`). You could then read that indent symbol to preserve indentation on existing files. It wouldn't be added to the resulting files as symbols aren't enumerable by default.

comments.author: y-hsgw
Sidnioulz
comments.body:
That's great, thank you so much!

Yes, this is what I had in mind. Using a symbol will make sure that JSON.stringify doesn't add the property to `packageJson` when printing.

comments.author: Sidnioulz
comments.body: One tiny thing though, when handling numbers, `??` is always better than `||` which would also match 0. In case someone has a 0-indentation file :sweat_smile:

comments.author: coderabbitai
comments.body:
_🛠️ Refactor suggestion_ | _🟠 Major_

**Avoid broadening all string keys to `any`; add only a symbol index signature**

`Record<string | symbol, any>` effectively de-types every property on `PackageJson` (string keys become `any`). Keep TypeFest’s strong typing and add a symbol index only.



Apply this diff:

```diff
-export type PackageJson = PackageJsonFromTypeFest & Record<string | symbol, any>;
+// Allow non-enumerable symbol metadata (e.g., indentation) without weakening string-keyed fields
+export type PackageJson = PackageJsonFromTypeFest & { [k: symbol]: unknown };
```

This preserves strict typing for known fields while enabling symbol metadata.

comments.author: ndelangen
comments.body: This feels rather hacky to me. I get that it works, but it's very unexpected behavior.

comments.author: Sidnioulz
comments.body:
It's probably gonna be less often wrong than it was before, and we use the same hack in the ESLint plugin so we're not increasing our maintenance surface wrt. dependencies.

I personally think it's nice to reformat a file after doing codegen on it, and this is likely as close as we can get without knowing what prettifier end users are using.

comments.author: ghengeveld
comments.body: I'm okay with this trick as long as it's clarified why this uses a Symbol. A code comment along the lines of "Using a Symbol key so JSON.stringify will omit it later" would suffice. It wasn't obvious to me that this is how stringify behaves, I had to manually verify.

There is no need to use `Symbol.for`. Just define it as a constant at the top of the file and reference that.
```suggestion
      return packageJson[indentSymbol];
```

With at the top of the file:
```js
const indentSymbol = Symbol('indent');
```
